title: Novel Isoquinoline Alkaloid Litcubanine A - A Potential Anti-Inflammatory Candidate.
authors: Xia, Huan; Liu, Yitong; Xia, Guiyang; Liu, Yi; Lin, Sheng; Guo, Lijia
one_liner_zh: 该文研究新型异喹啉生物碱LA的抗炎作用，涉及iNOS蛋白的分子对接，但核心是药物-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Macrophages play a critical role in innate and adaptive immunity, and the regulation of macrophage function in inflammatory disease treatment has been widely studied. Litsea cubeba is an important Chinese medicinal plant used for the treatment of inflammatory diseases. However, the inflammatory bioactive ingredients in L. cubeba and underlying molecular mechanisms are poorly understood. Herein, we first obtained and elucidated a novel isoquinoline alkaloid, Litcubanine A (LA), from L. cubeba. An in vitro study indicated that LA could significantly inhibit LPS-induced activation of inflammatory macrophages via the NF-kappaB pathway, leading to the decrease of inflammatory factors including iNOS, TNF-alpha, and IL-1beta. Moreover, LA showed an inhibiting effect on the expression of NO in macrophages by directly binding to iNOS protein. Molecular simulation docking also demonstrated that active LA created an interaction with GLU 371 residue of iNOS via attractive charge derived from the N-->O group, revealing its highly selective inhibition toward iNOS. By using the IkappaK inhibitor and iNOS inhibitor, these two regulatory targets of LA on inflammatory macrophages were verified in vitro. Finally, by using a caudal fin resection model in zebrafish larvae, and the skin wound healing model in mice, we proved in vivo that LA down-regulated the secretion of local inflammatory factors by inhibiting macrophage recruitment and activation at the early stage of the injury. Collectively, our study demonstrated that the novel isoquinoline alkaloid LA suppresses LPS-induced activation of inflammatory macrophages by modulating the NF-kappaB pathway, suggesting that inflammatory macrophage activation pathway is an effective target for inflammation treatment, and LA is a new pharmacophore for the development of novel and effective anti-inflammatory agents to regulate local macrophages.
abstract_zh: 巨噬细胞在先天性和适应性免疫中发挥关键作用，其在炎症性疾病治疗中的功能调控已被广泛研究。山鸡椒（Litsea cubeba）是一种重要的中药植物，用于治疗炎症性疾病。然而，山鸡椒中的炎症生物活性成分及其潜在分子机制尚不清楚。在此，我们首次从山鸡椒中获取并阐明了一种新型异喹啉生物碱——山鸡椒碱A（Litcubanine A, LA）。体外研究表明，LA可通过NF-κB通路显著抑制脂多糖（LPS）诱导的炎症巨噬细胞活化，导致包括iNOS、TNF-α和IL-1β在内的炎症因子减少。此外，LA通过直接结合iNOS蛋白，对巨噬细胞中NO的表达表现出抑制作用。分子模拟对接也表明，活性LA通过N→O基团产生的吸引电荷与iNOS的GLU 371残基发生相互作用，揭示其对iNOS的高度选择性抑制。通过使用IκB激酶抑制剂和iNOS抑制剂，我们在体外验证了LA对炎症巨噬细胞的这两个调控靶点。最后，利用斑马鱼幼鱼尾鳍切除模型和小鼠皮肤伤口愈合模型，我们在体内证明LA通过抑制损伤早期巨噬细胞的募集和活化，下调局部炎症因子的分泌。总体而言，我们的研究表明，新型异喹啉生物碱LA通过调节NF-κB通路抑制LPS诱导的炎症巨噬细胞活化，提示炎症巨噬细胞活化通路是炎症治疗的有效靶点，且LA是开发新型有效抗炎药物以调控局部巨噬细胞的新药效团。
